1.explanation: All of the XML parsing and highlighting rules live in src/languages/xml.js. In that file the regular expression for tag names with namespace prefixes was updated in v10.4.0 to require at least two characters before the colon, so single-letter prefixes no longer match. To fix this bug you need to adjust the namespace-prefix pattern in xml.js (e.g. allow `\w` or `[A-Za-z]` of length ≥1 before the colon) so that tags like `<a:OK>` are highlighted correctly.
1.bug_scenario: When using the XML mode in highlight.js (via the highlight API), multi-letter namespace prefixes (e.g. abc:OK, ab:OK) are highlighted correctly, but a single-letter prefix like a:OK is not recognized and its tag name stays un-highlighted. The screenshots show that any element with a:… prefix is rendered as plain text even when nested, whereas prefixes of length ≥2 still get proper syntax coloring.

2.explanation: All XML/HTML/SVG highlighting rules live in src/languages/xml.js. The regex that matches qualified (namespaced) tag names currently forces the prefix to be two or more characters, so it never recognizes single-letter prefixes. By adjusting the tag-name pattern there (e.g. allowing one-char prefixes before the colon), single-letter namespaces will once again match and be highlighted correctly.
2.bug_scenario: The problem is that after upgrading to v10.4.0, XML tags with a single-letter namespace prefix no longer receive syntax highlighting. In the reproducer you can see that “<abc:OK …/>” and “<ab:OK …/>” still highlight correctly, but “<a:FAIL xmlns:a=“…”/>” renders in plain text (no coloring for the tag or prefix). The same breakage also appears when the single-letter-prefixed tag wraps nested elements. All multi-letter prefixes and default (no-prefix) tags continue to highlight as expected.
